My work combines psychophysics and behavioural experiments with statistical
methods and time-series analysis. The underlying question is how the nervous
system represents time, on scales ranging from milliseconds to 24 hours.

## Research lines

::: {.entry}
### Perception and production of temporal intervals
How we estimate, reproduce and synchronise intervals from milliseconds to
seconds: finger-tapping tasks, sensorimotor synchronisation, and the effect of
sensory context on temporal judgements.

[Tools and online experiments](https://github.com/spiousas?tab=repositories){.entry-meta}
:::

::: {.entry}
### Circadian rhythms and sleep
Estimating circadian phase from actigraphy, wearable and luminescence data;
markers such as the dim light melatonin onset (DLMO), and the effect of
daylight-saving transitions on sleep in real-world populations.

[CircaLuc: circadian luminescence analysis app](https://github.com/spiousas/CircaLuc){.entry-meta}
:::

::: {.entry}
### Auditory and spatial perception
Sound-source localisation, distance perception, and the interaction between
auditory and visual information in building perceptual space.
:::

::: {.entry}
### Statistical methods for the behavioural sciences
Inference for periodic data, mixed models and the analysis of experimental data
with R. Much of this work overlaps with my [teaching](teaching.qmd) and with the
[blog](blog.qmd).
:::
